title: Position 1 departure and return; return posture differed
goal: Measure whether a controlled operator departure and return produces a repeatable channel-amplitude change at one fixed Pluto position.
hypothesis: The operator leaving the room may alter amplitude transfer beyond repeated-burst variability; return toward the first response would support a scene-related effect.

ground_truth.presence: Operator-directed departure; timed B capture, user-confirmed return before C
ground_truth.return_pose: Operator subsequently reported a slightly different lean

environment: Pluto and stock antennas fixed near computer/router; operator controls chair/body position. No measured antenna geometry, exact displacement or bearing.
rf_chain: Stock TX/RX antennas attached directly to the fixed desk Pluto; no added amplifier. Antenna spacing, orientation and calibrated gains unmeasured.
calibration_state: No calibrated RF gain, path delay, EIRP or absolute phase. Capture delay/common phase treated as nuisance parameters; amplitude retained.
clock_state: Existing Pluto clock configuration retained, no external reference configured; readback sample rate 4999999 samples/s.

stages: B: operator outside room; chair/device/final door position unchanged
C: returned and settled at original seated position
protocol.analysis: Compare absolute digital transfer amplitude and frequency-dependent amplitude shape; account for timing and carrier-phase nuisance independently per burst. No conversion to range.

success_criteria: Describe B change relative to burst variability and check C return. One A/B/A cycle is exploratory; without a return or if change is within repeat variability, attribution is inconclusive.
No clipping, FIFO overflow or watchdog expiry; final TX muted and RX restored
authorization_and_limits: User-authorized low-power laboratory operation, excluding cellular, GNSS and occupied spectrum. Only the previously surveyed 5771.5 MHz window was used with fresh receive-only guards, 45 dB hardware attenuation, digital backoff and a 0.8-second per-burst mute timer. Finite listening does not establish permanent vacancy; radiated power was not calibrated.
code_identity: Exact capture source snapshots and SHA-256 in run record; offline feature replay and hashes verified.

results.interpretation: Inconclusive presence effect: return posture differed, and C did not recover the A baseline. No room geometry inferred.

failures: Return condition did not reproduce baseline pose: operator reported a different lean.
Return did not recover original amplitude baseline.
Capture metadata overstates operator confirmation for the timed B stage; corrected in a separate operator-events annotation while preserving originals.
suspected_causes: Changed posture may affect the measured channel.
Unmeasured hardware/calibration drift and ambient changes may contribute. No cause isolated.
uncertainties: One nonrandomized cycle with technical burst repeats
No independent occupancy, pose or door-position sensor
Same RX LO/gain rewritten for each guard; internal calibration continuity not measured
Uncalibrated direct coupling plus unresolved multipath
No measured range or bearing from this fixed antenna pair
remedies: Repeat multiple cycles with marked posture and matching timings.
Interleave seated-to-seated controls to characterize drift without a departure.
next_test: Matched-pose controlled repeats before interpreting a presence effect; room geometry requires additional measurements or constraints.
